title: Localization of modules is exact
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $T\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset. For an $R$-module $P$ let $T^{-1}P$ be its localization (fractions $p/t$, $p\in P$, $t\in T$, with $p/t=p'/t'$ iff $u(t'p-tp')=0$ for some $u\in T$) and for an $R$-linear $h:P\to P'$ let $T^{-1}h:T^{-1}P\to T^{-1}P'$, $p/t\mapsto h(p)/t$. If $L\xrightarrow{u}M\xrightarrow{v}N$ is an exact sequence of $R$-modules ($\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$), then $T^{-1}L\xrightarrow{T^{-1}u}T^{-1}M\xrightarrow{T^{-1}v}T^{-1}N$ is exact.
